verification_scope_reason: Actual mounted native executor delegates to shared scheduling rather than another scheduler copy. Batches retain the provider's pipeline, support absent Agent and optional log, carry resolved admission, commit results/context in model order, aggregate successful turn conclusion, use exclusive barriers or bounded parallel pools, and honor a batch override over provider limit=1. Invalid overrides reject before batch dispatch. Cancellation distinguishes invoked/skipped calls. Actual V4 Session writes use tool-role messages; a real result append failure returns ToolBatchExecutionError with exact cause and only the successfully committed prefix. Existing scheduling failure consumers exercise started-call drainage and first-failure preservation on the same shared implementation.
initial_findings: The first observer assumed a nested result callId rather than toolCallId. It also prepared a Source Session without entering/announcing it, which correctly rejected writes. Corrected those fixtures and added the required V4 tool-message provider/consumer adaptation; legacy V3 creation stays unchanged. Initial logs remain preserved.
activation_boundary: Native batch provider and V4 durable result consumer qualified for these journeys. Agent loop still needs admission ownership, context refresh, current executor dispatch and partial-failure recovery. PTC bindings, model adapters and coordinated composition are not certified here. Production pin and accepted_upstream remain unchanged.
retained_assets: Commands, logs, XML and JSON observations retained. No task test process remains; shared fixed Source and toolchain retained through C9.
